messages:
Marta L: Quick heads-up — ran the TP baseline with the updated kernel selector + minislice batching. Observing an all-reduce tail on the 8xA100 run around the 200KB total per-op window. p95 spikes ~3x for some microbatches.

Kevin H: Can you drop the perf logs / flamegraph link? cc @Ryan C

Marta L: Paste below small excerpt from the trace and a link: https://perf.internal/runs/3245 — short summary:
- step 420: allreduce wall 72ms (expected ~22ms)
- per-rank payload reported by runtime: 23.7KB
- runtime policy picked NCCL ring path (policy threshold msgsize >= 128KB)

Marta L: Profiling snippet (nvprof-like):
```
COMM_ALLREDUCE start 0x7f..  payload_bytes=189600 total_msgs=8
ncclRingAllReduce time=68.3ms, bandwidth=12.4GB/s
treeReduce fallback none
kernel_selector: chosen=ring_kv_coalesce_v2
```

Ryan C: Wait — runtime compares the aggregate message size, right? if it used aggregate >128KB it forced ring, but actual per-chunk after fragmenting for the KV cache is ~24KB. That makes ring suboptimal for latency due to extra handshake rounds.

Devon S: Also saw this pattern earlier when KV cache hit rates fluctuate. If prefix cache invalidation makes each rank send slightly different prefixes, fragmentation increases commshape variance -> harms rings because they assume uniform chunking.

Kevin H: Did you try forcing the tree algorithm for the same run? Any diff?

Marta L: I ran a quick A/B: forced tree for the same commit/inputs. Results: p50 -6%, p95 -28%, tail reduced a lot. Ran three 100-step repeats.

Marta L: Quick numbers:
- Ring (baseline): p50=18.6ms, p95=72.3ms
- Tree (forced): p50=17.4ms, p95=52.1ms
(8-GPU TP layout, same kernel scheduling)

Ryan C: Interesting. That suggests kernel_selector policy needs to consider per-rank fragment size (post-coalesce) rather than aggregate. Kernel heuristics are using msgsize histograms that are computed before KV coalescing?

Marta L: Right now we compute expected_msg = batch_bytes / gpus and compare to thresholds. But minislice batching + KV coalesce changes the effective per-message shape.

Devon S: Proposed heuristic: compute commshape = median(fragment_size_per_rank) during the planning window, and pick tree if commshape < 64KB OR high variance across ranks. Also add a guard: if kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.85, prefer tree for latency-sensitive routes.

Kevin H: Can you capture NCCL counters (collectives, Rendezvous vs P2P steps) and GPU PCIe vs NVLink breakdown? Might reveal extra PCIe hops for ring path.

Marta L: Pasted minimal counter dump:
```
nccl_coll_count(allReduce)=820
nccl_ring_steps_avg=6.1
nvlink_transfers=1.2GB/s per link
pci_transfers=0.9GB/s (spike during tail)
```

ci-bot: deploy-benchmark: run 3245 completed for commit abc123 — perf regression alert triggered (delta p95 +22%).

Kevin H: OK action items:
1) Marta + Ryan: add per-fragment commshape metric to the runtime telemetry and bake into kernel_selector.
2) Devon: add kv_cache_hit_rate telemetry and expose as input to selector.
3) Marta: run targeted microbench: nccl-tests allreduce with simulated fragment sizes [8KB, 24KB, 64KB, 200KB] on the TP layout and capture ring vs tree. Post results to the perf run.
4) Open a bug for selector policy change and flag this regression for the recent minislice batching change (link ticket: PERF-7721).

Marta L: Will start microbench now and upload traces. Leaving notes in PERF-7721 with sample commands:
```
# microbench helper
python tools/commshape.py --layout tp8 --algo allreduce --sizes 8192,24576,65536,200000 --repeat 30 --collect nvprof
```

Ryan C: Thanks — if tree wins consistently for <64KB fragments we should add an autoswitch heuristic and a canary that flips selector for 5% of traffic.

Devon S: Adding KV-cache flagged metric to rollout checklist. Also check if quantized/offload path changes fragmentation.

Marta L: Cool. I'll attach flamegraphs + csv of per-step commshape when done. :thumbsup:
